os_version: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Apple Silicon, live user session

stack_detection.method: app is AppleScript-scriptable (sdef present); Apple Events consent granted

channel_setup: Apple Events consent (one TCC dialog per host→app pair, granted by the user once). AppleScript 'body text of document 1' as the macOS analog of the Windows COM / LibreOffice UNO document-model channel.

t1_read_text.detail: Known sentence set then read back char-exact (accents, em-dash, 🦊) in 73 ms round-trip. REMARKABLE: object-model reads AND writes kept working while the session was LOCKED (screen on loginwindow) — the same moment AX was returning degenerate/empty trees. Channels have different failure modes; a router can exploit that.

t2_enumerate.detail: Object model addresses document structure (paragraphs, character ranges), not on-screen controls — no bounding boxes at all. The channel is semantic but COORDINATE-FREE: it cannot aim a click; must be paired with AX for geometry.

t3_live_value.detail: Two variants: (a) pure object-model write+read: 158 ms, exact; (b) real keyboard input via CGEvents → the typed marker appeared in 'body text' read via AppleScript (114 ms). The AX-side cross-read of (b) was INCONCLUSIVE due to a probe-side hazard worth recording: the cached AXTextArea handle had gone transient after UI churn (frame width 1.25 px — a caret-like remnant) and its AXValue lacked the marker; the earlier fresh walk did contain the full body text. Lesson: re-resolve AX element handles immediately before every read/act; stale handles read stale/void content without erroring.

t4_living_screen.detail: No self-updating region in a static document.

t5_blind_action.detail: Not applicable to a coordinate-free channel (see t2).

t6_pictorial.detail: Not run (no image inserted in this cell; TextEdit cell covers AX-side image declaration).

measurements.notes: view = the document body itself (82 bytes for the probe sentence) — the object model returns EXACTLY the semantic content, zero UI noise; contrast with the AX view of the same window: 93 nodes / 11.2 KB (and see below). Window 1016×949 logical → 1285 screenshot tokens; the actual 2× capture (2032×1898 px) costs 4784 after the API's automatic downscale, not 5142. Latency: 73–158 ms per AppleScript round-trip (osascript process spawn included) — 30–70× slower than an in-process AX attribute read, but each call replaces an entire screenshot+OCR pass. AX-side contrast for the same app: the document body was ABSENT from AX (explicit — no AXLayoutArea at all) until the same AT-latch poke as Safari/Chrome flipped it (AXEnhancedUserInterface set → error -25208 → content appears anyway a beat later): THREE engines (Chromium, WebKit, iWork) gate their AX behind assistive-client detection. Under session lock, AXWindows returned the app's menu tree instead of windows (833-node degenerate view) while the object model was unaffected.

runtime_verification.method: Dual-channel agreement: object-model body text vs AX AXTextArea value (after AT-latch), vs native window screenshot artifact.
runtime_verification.agreement: Object-model ↔ screen: exact. AX ↔ object-model: exact on fresh handles; a stale transient handle disagreed (probe artifact, documented in t3) — re-resolve handles before use.

permissions_required: Apple Events (Automation) consent for Terminal→Pages — one user click
Accessibility TCC only for the AX cross-checks, not for the channel itself
